tasks.description: Implement sandbox/egg_agent_tools/tools/ with one module per namespace. Each tool registration also declares a cli_command attribute when a shell CLI counterpart exists (e.g. cli_command=('egg-orch','consensus','propose') for brc_propose); tools without a CLI counterpart (brc_get_state, brc_list_blocking, phase_get_context, phase_get_assigned_tasks, check_hitl_answers) omit cli_command or set it to None. decisions.question: Which approach should we adopt for exposing egg CLIs to sandbox agents?

options.label: A: Auto-generated AGENT-TOOLS.md + improved --help (status quo polish)
B: Tool manifest rendered into system prompt at spawn time
C: Second orchestrator-hosted MCP server (streamable HTTP) scoped to sandbox agents
D: In-process SDK MCP server via create_sdk_mcp_server + @tool decorators, wired into egg_agent.client (Recommended)
Hybrid D+B: in-process SDK tools as primary surface, plus a short tool index injected into the system prompt
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Hybrid D+B: in-process SDK tools as primary surface, plus a short tool index injected into the system prompt"}

decisions.question: Should the MCP tool surface be auto-generated from CLI argparse introspection, or hand-curated?

options.label: Auto-generated: single source of truth is each CLI's argparse; new subcommands surface automatically (matches AC 'no doc drift')
Hand-curated: explicit @tool definitions with hand-written descriptions/schemas; tighter quality, but risks drift
Hybrid: auto-generate the skeleton, allow per-tool overrides for descriptions/schemas where the argparse help is insufficient (Recommended)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Hybrid: auto-generate the skeleton, allow per-tool overrides for descriptions/schemas where the argparse help is insufficient (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Must the solution also cover the experimental 'egg' harness (EGG_HARNESS=egg), or claude_agent_sdk only for now?

options.label: claude_agent_sdk harness only — the egg harness is opt-in and experimental; parallel registration can be added later when it graduates (Recommended)
Both harnesses from day one — register the same tool handlers in both egg_agent.client (SDK) and shared/egg_harness/tools (egg harness registry)
Only the egg harness — treat this as the forcing function to migrate sandbox agents onto the new harness
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "claude_agent_sdk harness only — the egg harness is opt-in and experimental; parallel registration can be added later when it graduates (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Should the existing shell CLIs under sandbox/bin/egg-* remain as first-class, or be deprecated once the MCP tool surface lands?

options.label: Keep both indefinitely — CLIs are used by humans, tests, entrypoint scripts, and bash wrappers; MCP tools are additive for agents (Recommended — matches AC 'existing CLIs keep working')
Keep CLIs, but soft-deprecate with a banner that points agents at the MCP tool when one is available
Remove CLIs as we finish each MCP tool; force agents onto the structured surface
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Keep both indefinitely — CLIs are used by humans, tests, entrypoint scripts, and bash wrappers; MCP tools are additive for agents (Recommended — matches AC 'existing CLIs keep working')"}

decisions.question: How should MCP tools be named so agents can pattern-match them quickly?

options.label: Flat namespace under one server: mcp__egg__contract_add_decision, mcp__egg__orch_pipeline_status, mcp__egg__checkpoint_search (one server, flat names)
Per-CLI servers: mcp__egg_contract__add_decision, mcp__egg_orch__pipeline_status, etc. (one SDK server per CLI binary) (Recommended — mirrors the CLI surface the humans already know)
Subcommand-join form: mcp__egg__contract/add-decision (preserve the exact shell command as the tool name suffix)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Superseded by decision-7 in the v5 analysis draft: semantic verbs grouped by function (what the agent is DOING), not CLI taxonomy. Names like mcp__sdlc__register_open_question, mcp__brc__propose, mcp__phase__get_context. This decision (decision-5) was framed around CLI-mirroring options and is obsolete."}

decisions.question: What is the tool-surface scope — all subcommands of every egg CLI, or a curated high-value subset?

options.label: Everything — every subcommand of egg-contract, egg-orch, egg-checkpoint, egg-pipeline-watch, egg-sdlc, egg-health-inspect, egg-onboarding-docs becomes an MCP tool (maximizes discoverability, matches AC 'new CLI shows up automatically')

High-value subset first — only the subcommands agents hit in their BRC lifecycle (consensus propose/ack/nack/confirmed, message send/poll, contract add-decision/add-feedback/complete-task/update-notes, decision resolve, phase get/advance, anchor ops); expand iteratively (Recommended)
BRC-only — just the subcommands the PROPOSE/ACK/NACK/CONFIRM lifecycle depends on; all others stay shell-only
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Superseded by decision-8 in the v5 analysis draft: scope is defined by the Agent Capability Audit, not by CLI subcommand taxonomy. Iteration 1 ships the BRC + HITL core (~15 verbs: producer/reviewer lifecycle, HITL registration, heartbeat/progress, task completion, phase context orientation). Iteration 2 covers the remaining ~15 verbs from the full audit, tracked in issue #1917."}

decisions.question: How should MCP tools be named so agents can pattern-match them quickly? (Supersedes decision-5 after re-framing; decision-5 had CLI-taxonomy options and is superseded by the semantic-names recommendation.)

options.label: Semantic / verb-based names grouped by agent function, decoupled from CLI taxonomy — e.g. mcp__sdlc__register_open_question, mcp__brc__propose, mcp__phase__get_context, mcp__checkpoint__search. New capabilities with no CLI counterpart slot in naturally. Stable under CLI refactors. (Recommended)
CLI-mirroring names — mcp__egg_contract__add_decision, mcp__egg_orch__consensus_propose, one SDK server per CLI binary. Mirrors the shell surface humans know.
Flat namespace under one server — mcp__egg__contract_add_decision, mcp__egg__orch_consensus_propose (one server, flat names)
Subcommand-join form — mcp__egg__contract/add-decision (preserves exact shell command suffix)
Other (explain in reply)

New capabilities with no CLI counterpart slot in naturally. Stable under CLI refactors. (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: What is the iteration-1 agent-facing tool set? (Supersedes decision-6 after re-framing; decision-6 options were phrased as 'which CLI subcommands to cover' and are superseded by the capability-audit-driven scoping.)

decisions.question: [Phase gate: refine] The refine phase has completed. Please review the analysis and approve to continue, or provide feedback to request changes.

options.label: approve
request changes

decisions.resolution:
## Resolved Questions (captured for downstream phases)

**decision-1 (mechanism)**: Hybrid D + prompt nudge — in-process SDK MCP server via create_sdk_mcp_server + @tool, wired into egg_agent.client, plus a short system-prompt paragraph pointing agents at the mcp__* tools.

**decision-2 (handler derivation)**: Hybrid — auto-derive the skeleton from existing CLI/argparse-style signatures, allow per-tool overrides for descriptions/schemas where auto-derivation is insufficient.

**decision-3 (harness coverage)**: claude_agent_sdk harness only for iteration 1. Defer parallel registration for experimental EGG_HARNESS=egg until that harness graduates.

**decision-4 (CLI retention)**: Keep the sandbox/bin/egg-* CLIs indefinitely. Humans, tests, entrypoint scripts, and bash recovery wrappers depend on them; MCP tools are additive for agents. Do not deprecate.

**decision-7 (naming; supersedes decision-5)**: Semantic verbs grouped by function (what the agent is DOING). Examples: mcp__sdlc__register_open_question, mcp__brc__propose, mcp__phase__get_context. Rationale: agent's mental model is verbs; tool names are stable under CLI refactoring; capabilities with no CLI counterpart slot in naturally.

**decision-8 (scope; supersedes decision-6)**: BRC + HITL core for iteration 1 (~15 verbs): producer/reviewer lifecycle, HITL registration, heartbeat/progress, task completion, phase context orientation. Full capability audit (~30 verbs) is scoped to iteration 2 — tracked separately in issue #1917.

## Related issues filed during this refine

- #1915 — change_approach feedback via provide_input never reaches agents (found during this refine; workaround is direct send_message after reset)
- #1917 — iteration 2 follow-up for the remaining ~15 verbs from the full capability audit

## Notes for the plan phase

The agent-first framing is the authoritative frame; do not regress to CLI-taxonomy-based thinking. Name tools from the agent's perspective. If plan surfaces a verb that was missed in the refine capability audit, add it to the iteration-1 scope (if clearly core) or defer to #1917 (if optional).

pr.title: Expose egg agent capabilities as in-process SDK MCP tools
pr.description:
Sandbox agents currently spend a visible fraction of their turn
budget on tooling archaeology — `cat`-ing egg CLI binaries,
grepping for subcommand names, and reading Python source to
figure out how to invoke `egg-contract add-decision` or
`egg-orch consensus propose`. Issue #1765 documents a
refine-phase example where the agent burned five tool calls
before any productive work. The refine analysis at
`.egg-state/drafts/1765-analysis.md` evaluated four mechanisms
(polished docs, system-prompt manifest, second orchestrator MCP
server, in-process SDK MCP) and the HITL gate selected **Hybrid
D+B — in-process SDK MCP + short prompt nudge** — because it
gives agents typed, validated tools on the same `tool_use`
stream they already handle, with zero new network surface and
no new auth layer.

## Changes

1. **New package `sandbox/egg_agent_tools/`** (handlers, tools,
   schemas, server factory). The 15 iteration-1 verbs land as
   pure handler functions in `handlers/*.py` and as
   `@tool`-decorated SDK wrappers in `tools/*.py`. Namespaces
   are semantic (not CLI-mirroring) per decision-7:
   `mcp__sdlc__*` (3 tools), `mcp__brc__*` (6), `mcp__phase__*`
   (2), `mcp__progress__*` (3), `mcp__task__*` (1).
2. **Refactor existing `cmd_*` functions** in
   `sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py` and
   `sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py` to call the shared handlers.
   Argparse surface, stdout text, and exit codes unchanged —
   humans, tests, and bash scripts see zero behaviour change.
3. **Wire `shared/egg_agent/client.py::run_agent_async`** to
   build an in-process MCP server via
   `claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server` and set it on
   `ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers` when `EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true`.
   Also append a ≤200-word bootstrap paragraph to
   `options.system_prompt` when the flag is on.
4. **CI drift test** asserts every MCP tool with a declared CLI
   counterpart dispatches the same handler module function as
   the CLI argparse — schema/behaviour drift is impossible by
   construction.
5. **Feature-flag gated rollout** via `EGG_MCP_TOOLS` env var
   (default `false`). Off-path is byte-identical to today. A
   follow-up issue will track burn-in and flip the default.
6. **Docs and rule updates** so operators know how to opt in and
   agents know the tools exist.
7. **SDK pin + smoke test.** `claude-agent-sdk` is pinned to a
   bounded range (`>=0.1.65,<0.2`) in `sandbox/pyproject.toml`
   and the `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION` ARG in
   `sandbox/Dockerfile`, with an import-time smoke test so a
   future pre-1.0 bump fails CI loudly instead of silently
   breaking every sandbox.
8. **Async + error discipline.** Handlers raise exceptions (no
   `sys.exit`); `@tool` wrappers run handlers via
   `asyncio.to_thread` and wrap exceptions as structured
   tool-result error blocks. A gateway flake surfaces as a
   tool error, never an agent crash. The existing CLI surface
   keeps its `sys.exit` behaviour by catching the same
   exceptions in the `cmd_*` shim.

## Impact

Opted-in agents see 15 typed, validated `mcp__*` tools in their
first tool_use block and can invoke BRC propose/ACK/NACK,
register HITL decisions, request feedback, emit progress, and
fetch phase context without shelling out to `egg-orch` or
`egg-contract`. Non-opt-in pipelines are unchanged. Existing
`sandbox/bin/egg-*` CLIs keep working for humans, tests, and
bash recovery scripts (decision-4). The experimental
`EGG_HARNESS=egg` path is unaffected in iteration 1
(decision-3) and tracked for parallel registration when the
harness graduates. The remaining ~15 capability-audit verbs
(peer, checkpoint, anchor, overseer) are out of scope for this
PR and tracked in #1917.
pr.test_plan:
- Automated unit tests (`tests/sandbox/egg_agent_tools/`): every
  handler exercised for happy-path, missing-arg, and 5xx-gateway
  scenarios — the error test asserts the handler raises
  GatewayError (not sys.exit). Every @tool wrapper tested for
  (a) JSON-serialised handler response on success, (b) is_error
  structured tool-result on handler exception (so a gateway
  flake never surfaces as an agent crash). `test_server.py`
  verifies `build_sandbox_mcp_server` registers the 15 expected
  tool names and SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE is symmetrically derived
  from TOOL_NAMESPACES (drift test catches extra or missing
  namespaces in either direction).
- Automated client tests (`tests/shared/egg_agent/test_client.py`):
  `EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true` wires `mcp_servers['egg']` on
  `ClaudeAgentOptions` and appends the nudge; flag-unset yields
  byte-identical options; `can_use_tool` callback passes
  `mcp__*` tool names through (does not spuriously block).
- Automated CLI parity tests (`tests/sandbox/test_contract_cli.py`,
  `tests/sandbox/test_orch_cli.py`): every refactored `cmd_*`
  asserted against committed inline stdout/exit-code fixtures
  (no first-run auto-record); error-path test confirms
  `cmd_*` catches `GatewayError` and renders the same stderr +
  exit code humans see today.
- Automated drift CI test (`tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py`):
  every tool with a declared `cli_command` attribute dispatches
  the same handler module function as the CLI's `cmd_*` — fails
  CI if they diverge.
- Automated SDK-pin smoke test
  (`tests/sandbox/egg_agent_tools/test_sdk_surface.py`): imports
  `claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server` and
  `claude_agent_sdk.tool` at module load time; fails loudly on
  an incompatible SDK upgrade.
- Automated integration test
  (`integration_tests/test_sandbox_mcp_tools_e2e.py`, marker-
  gated): spawns the SDK with `EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true` and asserts
  the agent's first tool_use block names an `mcp__*` tool (not
  Bash). Catches SDK API drift the offline mocks cannot.
- Manual: run one pipeline with `EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true` and
  confirm the refiner's first tool_use block contains
  `mcp__brc__propose`, `mcp__sdlc__register_open_question`,
  etc., not `Bash /opt/egg-runtime/sandbox/bin/egg-contract`.
  Run one pipeline with the flag unset and confirm parity with
  today. Exercise one full NACK→fix→re-propose cycle to confirm
  `mcp__brc__nack` / `mcp__brc__propose` / `mcp__brc__confirm`
  interoperate with other agents still on shell-CLI path.

Pre-merge: reviewer sets `EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true` on at least one

Post-merge: open a follow-up issue tracking the burn-in window

questions.question: Access-control slice: if we DO add a separate sandbox-facing MCP server (Option C), what's the minimum tool set we want exposed, and which orchestrator-side tools (submit_task / cancel_task / restart_phase / advance_phase / get_consensus_status) should NEVER be reachable from inside a sandbox? Is there a concrete threat model you want us to design against?
questions.answer: Moot — we chose Option D (in-process SDK MCP), not Option C. For the record: if Option C were revisited, the sandbox-facing server should expose only the BRC + HITL + phase-context core (~15 verbs per decision-11), and must NEVER expose submit_task, cancel_task, restart_phase, advance_phase, populate_contract, or the container/pod admin surface. Threat model to design against: a compromised sandbox container should not be able to (a) spawn or cancel pipelines, (b) modify other pipelines' state, (c) read checkpoints from other pipelines, or (d) escalate privilege by invoking orchestrator admin APIs. Option D sidesteps this by construction — handlers don't exist in the agent's process — so the threat-model work is deferred until/unless Option C is reconsidered.

questions.question: Drift-prevention contract: what's the acceptable mechanism for keeping the CLI and the tool schemas in sync? Options: (a) CI test that parses each CLI's argparse and diffs against the @tool registry; (b) single source of truth (argparse) with tools derived at import time; (c) make the CLI a thin wrapper over the @tool functions (CLI calls the same handler internally). Which flavour of 'no drift' do you want?
questions.answer: Flavour (c): make the CLI a thin wrapper over the @tool handler functions. Both the shell CLI and the MCP tool dispatch into the same handler — single source of truth, no drift possible by construction. This aligns with decision-2's hybrid auto+override (argparse defines the skeleton schema; handlers define the behavior). Add (a) as belt-and-suspenders: a CI test that asserts every @tool has a matching CLI subparser for any tool that is expected to be CLI-accessible, and vice versa. Rejecting (b) standalone: 'argparse as single source of truth' can't express the new verbs (brc_get_state as JSON, peer_read_artifact, etc.) that have no CLI equivalent — the tool registry is the authoritative surface, not argparse.

questions.question: Bootstrap guidance: even after MCP tools are registered, should we inject a short (<=200 word) 'these tools exist, prefer them over Bash' paragraph into the system prompt, or trust the SDK's native tool-discovery without a prompt nudge? Past experience suggests agents sometimes default to Bash even when a structured tool exists.
questions.answer: Yes — inject a short (<=200 word) bootstrap paragraph into the system prompt per decision-10/7 (Hybrid D + prompt nudge). The paragraph should name the tool namespaces (mcp__sdlc__*, mcp__brc__*, mcp__phase__*, mcp__progress__*) and explicitly say 'prefer these over Bash for agent-lifecycle operations.' Past experience (cited in the draft) shows agents default to Bash even when a structured tool exists; the prompt nudge corrects for that without spending prompt tokens on full tool schemas.

questions.question: Output shape for diagnostic subcommands: commands like 'egg-orch pipeline status' emit rich terminal tables/JSON. Should the MCP tool return (a) the JSON payload verbatim, (b) a compact text summary for token economy, or (c) both as multi-content blocks? This affects tool-call token cost and agent comprehension.
questions.answer: JSON payload verbatim (option a). Typed tools should return structured data; agents will parse JSON reliably with orders of magnitude fewer errors than parsing terminal-table output. Token-economy argument for compact text is weak because tool results are not billed per input token in the agent's steady-state loop. If a human-formatted view is useful for something else (e.g., debug checkpoint replay), generate it separately from the CLI, not from the MCP tool. Exception: for very large payloads (brc_get_state on a pipeline with dozens of agents), tools should accept a `verbose: bool` argument and default to a compact projection.

questions.question: Authn/authz for network-transport MCP (if Option C lands instead of D): sandbox agents currently authenticate to the gateway via EGG_SESSION_TOKEN. Should a sandbox-facing MCP server reuse that token, introduce a new per-agent token, or piggyback on the existing EGG_LIFECYCLE_SECRET? What's the expected token lifecycle across agent restarts?
questions.answer: N/A — we chose Option D, which runs tools in the agent's own process. No new auth layer is needed because handlers execute inside the sandbox's existing trust boundary. This question becomes relevant only if we revisit Option C in a future iteration.

questions.question: Observability: should MCP tool calls generate distinct log events / checkpoints separate from the SDK's built-in tool_use stream? Today, Bash calls to egg CLIs show up as 'Bash' tool_use blocks in checkpoints; if they become first-class MCP tools they'll show up under distinct names — does the checkpoint browser need any changes to group or search them?
questions.answer: MCP tool calls get distinct names natively (`mcp__sdlc__register_open_question` vs `Bash`) in the tool_use stream — the checkpoint browser will show them correctly without any code changes. Optional future improvement: add a checkpoint-search facet to filter by MCP-tool namespace prefix (mcp__sdlc__*, mcp__brc__*, etc.) for analytics; not required for iteration 1.

questions.question: Timeouts and cancellation: SDK MCP server tool calls default to 60s connection timeout; some egg subcommands (e.g. 'egg-pipeline-watch', 'egg-checkpoint search') can run longer. What's the right timeout envelope, and should long-running operations be split into start/poll tool pairs rather than blocking?
questions.answer: Default 60s timeout is fine for the BRC + HITL + phase-context core — these are all fast operations (register a decision, read a task list, propose a version, query current state). For long-running verbs in iteration 2 (checkpoint_search, overseer_query_status with deep history, peer_poll_messages with a long wait): split into start/poll pairs. Pattern: `<verb>_start` returns a job-id; `<verb>_poll(job_id)` returns result-or-still-running. This also gives the agent a natural cancellation point. Not a concern for iteration 1 since none of the core 15 verbs are long-running.

questions.question: Rollout plan preference: should the MCP tool surface be enabled for all roles simultaneously, or gated behind a feature flag (e.g. EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true) during a burn-in window where we compare token/turn-count between the two modes?
questions.answer: Feature-flag gated initially (e.g., EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true in ClaudeAgentOptions.env or as a per-pipeline config). Burn-in window of N=5-10 pipelines comparing turn-count and cost-per-phase between MCP-enabled and shell-only modes. Flip default to ON once metrics show ≥15% reduction in turns-per-phase for the refine/plan phases (the ones with highest tooling-archaeology cost in #1765's motivating observation). Rollout feature flag can be removed in a follow-up after a clean week. This matches the pattern used in prior egg rollouts (overseer, concurrent-mode).
